title: Pairing claim response
description: POST /v1/pairing/requests/{id}/claim. On an approved request it returns the device credential together with the host identity the client pins: the certificate fingerprint and the addresses this host answers on. `grants` says which of the three things the one approval covers actually landed, and `ssh` is where the terminal lives so no user has to type it. A pending request returns the same shape without credential fields.

endpoints.description: TAIL-2 P0-2: every road to this host, each with its kind. `lan` addresses first (IPv4 before IPv6), then `<host_name>.local` (`mdns`), then the MagicDNS name and the tailnet addresses (`tailnet`, 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48). An iOS client can dial a tailnet road only by its MagicDNS name (ATS); it keeps the addresses to recognise a typed 100.x as this host. A client of a core before TAIL-2 receives no `kind` and infers it.

ssh_public_key.description: The single-line OpenSSH public key this request carried, if any.

grants.description: One approval, three grants. `companion` is this credential, `media` the Sunshine streaming certificate, `ssh` the authorized_keys line. A web client (LITE-1a) only ever gets `companion`.

ssh.description: Where this host's terminal is. The client fills its SSH surface from here instead of asking. TAIL-2 P0-4: `host` stays the first LAN address (what a client before TAIL-2 dials); `hosts` is every road with its kind, so a client connected over the tailnet dials the MagicDNS name. P1-1: `tailscale_ssh` is true when Tailscale SSH is on, which answers port 22 over the tailnet itself: Omodachi's key, its approval and a revoke here do not apply there.

remote_addr.description: The peer address the request arrived from, shown to whoever approves it. Null when the host could not read one. It is never authorization.

client.description: LITE-1a: what asked. `native` is the App; `web` is Odomo in a browser. A request that carried an `Origin` header is `web` whatever it said. `label` is the browser's own guess ("Safari on iPhone"), cleaned like a device name; null for the App.

client_label.description: LITE-1a: the approval card's words for a web client, formatted by core ("Web app · Safari on iPhone"). Null for the App.

via.description: The road the request came by (TAIL-2 P1-6) and who this host's own tailscaled says the peer is (`tailscale whois`): the node's short name and its owner's login (null for a tagged node, or when tailscaled cannot say). Behind `tailscale serve` (LITE-1a C3) the peer is the forwarded client, so a browser on the tailnet is `tailnet` like the App; when whois has no login, the `Tailscale-User-Login` serve added is used. Shown instead of a raw 100.x address. Context for the person approving, never authorization; null on a row written before TAIL-2.

already_paired.description: TAIL-2 P0-2: this device still held a live credential here when it asked (it forgot this host, or was reinstalled). The request waits for the same local Approve; the claim retires the older credentials with the renewal grace, so the device ends with one.

odomo_url.description: LITE-1b C7: Odomo's https address on the tailnet, from the `tailscale serve` mapping the installer recorded (443, or 8443 when 443 is somebody else's). Absent when there is none. Authenticated documents only; never on /health.

odomo.description: LITE-1d: Odomo for a native app deciding whether to offer it. `url` is `odomo_url` again (null when this host has no front door, i.e. no Tailscale serve mapping); `push_devices` is how many of this host's web devices hold a live push subscription that the person at the computer has not switched off, with a working credential. A count only: no device ids, no endpoints. Per host, not per person (core does not know who holds a device). Absent `push_devices`: this host cannot say (no push here). The whole object is absent when the host knows neither.
